results.content: # Convolutional LSTM. A Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) is a type of neural network that combines the convolutional and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) architectures, allowing for spatial dependencies in data sequences to be captured efficiently over time. AI generated definition based on: Medical Image Analysis, 2023. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are one of the most representative supervised deep learning approaches for modeling spatial or temporal correlations. During the training process, the model first extracts features from image data into convolution layers, which are then convolved using a filter with learnable weights. Next, in the pooling layer, the dimensionality of the input is reduced by subsampling (pooling) layers through a feature map size reduction method. Since traffic time series data from nodes in close proximity along the same link are likely to be related, multiple works have demonstrated the effectiveness of leveraging convolution-based DL models for extracting localized spatial dependencies from the multivariate time series data (Wu et al., 2018).
